CHOICE: 3
CONFIDENCE: 3

I did not verify this against the literature. The choice rests on recalling that stable stationary harmonic maps into spheres and compact Lie groups have singular sets of codimension at least 4, and that the excluded groups are the exceptions to that bound. Solution 1 is wrong because stable maps to S^2 can have codimension-3 singularities, so a universal bound of 5 fails. Solution 2 is unlikely because the map x/|x| composed into S^3 is probably unstable. Solution 3's sharpness argument is plausible but not checked in detail.
